en: בַּדָּד m. (denominative of בַּד II) olive-treader, workingman in the olive press. Gittin 62ᵃ.—plural בַּדָּדִין. Toharot X, 1 sq. Shabbat 19ᵇ שמן של ב׳ וכ׳ the oil (remnants in corners) belonging to the pressers, and the mats which they use. Bava Kamma 119ᵃ והב׳ לוקחין מהן וכ׳ (read מנשותיהן, see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l. note 40) you may buy from the oil pressers’ (Rashi: oil producers’) wives &c. Tosefta Ma'asrot I, 10 הב׳ (ה)מדליקין וכ׳ the oil pressers who take their lighting oil (alternately) from one press and another.

הֶיסֵּט, הֶסֵּט m. (יָסַט or סוּט) skaking an object so as to move it from its place, different interpretation or differently interpreted from רעדה vibration (see Tosefta Zavim IV, 6), especially hesset, one of the causes of levitical uncleanness. Toharot X, 1 אינן בקיאין בה׳ are not familiar with the laws of hesset. Megillah 8ᵇ מלטמא … בה׳ so as not to make earthen vessels unclean by shaking them; and from—plural הֶיסֵּיטוֹת, הֶסֵּטוֹת laws concerning hesset. Yerushalmi Demai II, 23ᵃ top. Yerushalmi Sotah V, 20ᵃ top.

sections.en: If one locked in olive-workers in the olive-press and there were objects in there that had midras uncleanness: Rabbi Meir says: the olive-press is deemed to be unclean. Rabbi Judah says: the olive-press remains clean. Rabbi Shimon says: if they regard them as clean, the olive-press is deemed unclean; but if they regard them as unclean,the olive-press remains clean. Rabbi Yose: why are they unclean? Only because the am haaretz is not an expert in the laws of hesset.
sections.he: הַנּוֹעֵל בֵּית הַבַּד מִפְּנֵי הַבַּדָּדִין וְהָיוּ לְשָׁם כֵּלִים טְמֵאִין מִדְרָס, רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, בֵּית הַבַּד טָמֵא. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, בֵּית הַבַּד טָהוֹר. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, אִם טְהוֹרִין לָהֶן, בֵּית הַבַּד טָמֵא. וְאִם טְמֵאִין לָהֶן, בֵּית הַבַּד טָהוֹר. אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, וְכִי מִפְּנֵי מָה טְמֵאוֹת, אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ בְּקִיאִין בְּהֶסֵּט:

en:
יָצָא (Biblical Hebrew)
1) to go forth; to rise (of the sun); to go out. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 39 אֵצֵא ויהיו וכ׳ I shall leave (my father’s house), and they may desecrate &c. Ib. י׳ לו מוניטון a medal was issued in his memory, see מוֹנִיטוֹן. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 6 בשעה שהוא יוצא when he (the sun) rises; בשעה שהיא יוֹצֵאת when she (the moon) rises. Sanhedrin 52ᵃ ארור שיָצָאת זו מחלציו (see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l. note) cursed is he from whose loins this woman went forth.—Shabbat V, 1 במה … יוֹצְאָה what is an animal permitted to wear on going out (on the Sabbath)? Ib. VI, 1 לא תֵצֵא וכ׳ a woman must not wear on going out &c.; and see from

—2) to end; to go to the end of, to live through. Yerushalmi Berakhot VIII, 12ᵇ bottom of page כיון שיָצָת שבת when the Sabbath ended. Yerushalmi Sheviit VI, 36ᶜ top אינו יוצא שבתו ולא יָ׳ וכ׳ he shall not live to the end of this week, and he did not arrive at the end of the week before he was dead; (Eruvin 63ᵃ הוציא שנתו, see infra); and e.

—3) to be expended. Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 14, end, see הוֹצָאָה.

—4) to be excluded; exempt; (rarely) to exclude, deduct. Yerushalmi Nedarim II, beginning 37ᵇ י׳ דבר של איסור this is to exclude a vow concerning a forbidden act; Bavli Nedarim 17ᵃ י׳ נשבע לבטל וכ׳ this excludes the case of one who makes oath that he will disregard a law. Yerushalmi Yevamot I, 2ᶜ top אשר תלד יָצְתָה זו וכ׳ ‘whom she may bear’ (Devarim XXV, 6), herewith is excluded she (the אַיְילוֹנִית) who &c.; and see from—Yerushalmi Chagigah I, 76ᶜ top צֵא מהם שני ימים deduct from them two days; ib. צא שבת מהם deduct the Sabbath day.—Esp. idiomatic uses: a) י׳ בן חורין, י׳ לחירות, or only י׳ to be freed. Peah III, 8; Gittin 42ᵃ. Kiddushin 24ᵃ יוצאבשן וכ׳ he is freed, when his master caused his loss of a tooth or an eye; and see from—b) (of a wife) to be sent away, to be divorced. Ketubot VII, 6 ואלו יוֹצְאוֹת שלא בכתובה the following wives have to leave without receiving their K’thubah. Ib. 7 תֵּצֵא she must leave. Ib. X, 5; and see from—c) י׳ ידי (or מִידֵי) to go out of the power of; to be released; to do justice to, be justified before. Shekalim III, 2 … לפי שאדם צריך לָצֵאת ידי הבריות לָצֵאת ידי המקום because man must appear justified before men as well as before God; Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 51; and from—י׳ ידי חובתו, or י׳ to comply with the requirements of the law. Berakhot 8ᵇ. Ib. II, 1 אם כיון לבו י׳ if he read with attention, he has done his duty (which requires the reading of the Sh’ma). Yerushalmi Shekalim III, 47ᵇ bottom of page מהו לצאת וכ׳ is the law complied with when one uses wine &c.?—Mekhilta Bo, Pisḥa, section (Parashah) 6; and see from—Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 39 לא יָצָאתָה ידי השבועה thou hast not redeemed thy oath; ib. section (Parashah) 49; Vayikra Rabbah section (Parashah) 10, beginning—Makhshirin VI, 5; Tosefta Toharot X, 3 י׳ מידי שמן, see מוֹחַל.—י׳ מידי פשוטו, see מִקְרָא.—d) י׳ מן הכלל or י׳ to be taken out of the general rule, to be specified (although being implied in the general rule). Sifra, introduction כל דבר שהיה בכלל וי׳ … לא ללמד על עצמו י׳ וכ׳ whatever would have been implied in the general law and yet is specified again (in the Biblical text) in order to teach (something not mentioned before), has been specified not only to teach something new concerning the specific case, but to teach it concerning the whole class. Ib. י׳ לטעון, see טָעַן I. Temurah I, 6 ולמה י׳ and for what purpose are tithes especially mentioned (Vayikra XXVII, 30, sq.)?; and from—e) כַּיּוֹצֵא ב־ like that which passes with it (in the same class), similar; in a similar way. Pesachim III, 2 אם יש כי׳ בו שהחמיץ if there is a similar dough (started simultaneously with the one in question) which has begun to ferment. Berakhot 59ᵇ, sq. ואין לו כי׳ בו when he has no house like it; כי׳ בהם garments like them. Zevachim V, 6 המורם מהם כי׳ בהם what is taken of them for the priest, is like them (subject to the same laws). Moʿed Katan 16ᵇ כי׳ בדבר אתה אומר וכ׳ in a similar way (as something coming under the same category) you read &c. Sifré Bamidbar 32; and see from—f) י׳ שכרו בהפסדו its benefit is lost in its disadvantage; i.e. benefit and disadvantage are counterbalanced. Pirkei Avot V, 11, sq.—g) (euphem.) to retire for human needs (see Toharot X, 2). Berakhot 62ᵃ השכם וצֵא וכ׳ go out early in the morning &c. Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 9 ואינו יוצא לנקביו and has no human needs. Ib. לא היה יוצא אלא וכ׳ he used to go out only to the water (to make believe he was a superhuman being); and from—h) to be proved, identified. Ketubot II, 3 היה כתב ידם יוצא ממקום אחר if their signature can be identified otherwise (than by their own declaration); and e.

Hifil - הוֹצִיא
1) to take out, to lead forth, bring forth; to release, discharge, send off. Berakhot VI, 1 before eating bread one says, המוֹצִיא לחם וכ׳ (blessed be thou, O Lord) who hast brought forth bread out of the earth (see ib. 38ᵃ as to המוציא or מוציא); ib. 37ᵇ; and from—Pirkei Avot Zar. 41ᵇ, and from אין ספק מוציא וכ׳, see וַדַּאי. Bava Metzia 37ᵇ לא זו הדרך מוֹצִיאָתוֹ מידי עבירה עד וכ׳ this is not the way that relieves him from sin (this is no full atonement), (he is not relieved) until he pays &c.; Yevamot XV, 7. Ib. 6, sq. אין זו דרך מוֹצִיאָתָהּ וכ׳ she is not relieved from the possibility of sin, unless she is not permitted to marry again and forbidden to partake of T’rumah.—Ib. 36ᵇ יוֹצִיא (יוֹצִיאָהּ) בגט he dismisses her with a letter of divorce. Ib. ואם נשא יוציא and if he married her (against the law), he must dismiss her (divorce her); and from—Pirkei Avot II, 11, and from מוֹצִיאִין את האדם מן העולם take a man out of the world, i.e. cause him to lose the true enjoyment of life.

—2) to exclude. Yerushalmi Yevamot I, 2ᶜ top איילונית מטעם אחר הוֹצֵאתָהּ the aylonith thou dost (the law does) exclude for another reason (see supra). Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 14, end אוֹצִיא את ישראל let me exclude the Israelites, א׳ את הזקנים the elders; and from—להוֹצִיא (= Chaldaic לאפוקי, see אַפֵּק, or למעוטי, see מעט) to the exclusion of. Sukkah 28ᵃ; Kiddushin 34ᵃ האזרח לה׳ את הנשים ‘the native’ (Vayikra XXIII, 42) intimates the exemption of women (from the duty of dwelling in booths); and see from

—3) to lead to the end, to live through. Eruvin 63ᵃ
, see supra.—4) to produce, present. Ketubot XIII, 8 המוציא שטר חוב … והלה ה׳ וכ׳ if one produces a note of indebtedness against his neighbor, and the latter produces evidence that the claimant sold him a field (and paid him, which he would not have done, if he had a claim). Ib. 9. Ib. IX, 9 הוֹצִיאָה גט
if she produces a letter of divorce; and see from—5) to spend, lay out. Ib. VIII, 5, see הוֹצָאָה; and from—Esp. idiomatic uses: a) ה׳ ידי חוב־ or ה׳ (see supra) to be the instrument of a person’s complying with the law, e.g. to read a prayer and thus cause the listener to perform his duty as though he read it himself; to act in another’s behalf effectively. Rosh Hashanah III, 5 אין מוֹצִיאִין את הרבים ידי חובתן they cannot act (blow the Shofar) in behalf of the assembled congregation. Ib. 29ᵃ אע"פ שיצא מוציא although he has done his duty (has read the prayer for himself), he may act in behalf of others. Ib. ולעצמו מוציא and can he (the half-slave and half-freedman) act in his own behalf?; and from—b) to collect, to claim. Ketubot VIII, 1 הבעל מוציא מיד הלקוחות the husband can reclaim the property from those who bought it. Bava Kamma III, 11 המוציא מחבירו עליו הראייה the claimant must produce evidence; and see from—c) to utter. Arakhin 5ᵃ, and from אין אדם מוציא דבריו לבטלה no man utters his words for no purpose (he must have meant something).—ה׳ לעז to slander, discredit. Shabbat 97ᵃ, and from, see לַעַז.—d) to carry an object (on the Sabbath) out of a private to a public place, or from one private place to another, see רָשׁוּת. Shabbat VII, 2, sq.; and from—e) to secrete. Sifré Bamidbar 88 יש לך … שאין מוציא וכ׳ is there a woman-born being that does not discharge the food he eats?; and e.—f) ה׳ שבת to dismiss the Sabbath with prayer, opposed הכניס. Shabbat 118ᵇ מוֹצִיאֵי שבת וכ׳ those who dismiss the Sabbath at Sepphoris.

פני, פָּנָה (Biblical Hebrew)
1) to turn (one’s face). Yoma 17ᵇ, and e. שאתה פוֹנֶה, see פִּינָּה. Yerushalmi Pirkei Avot Zar. III, 42ᵇ sq. (reference. to Vayikra XIX, 4) אל תִּפְנֶה לעובדן do not turn thy face to them to worship them; אל תפנה לראותן ממש it is meant literally, do not turn thy face to look at them; Sifra K’dosh. beginning אל תפנה לראותם וַדַּיי. Ib. תחלתם אלילים הם אם פּוֹנֶה את אחריהן וכ׳ at first they are ‘nothings’, but if thou turnest after them, thou wilt make them (thy) gods; Yalkut Vayikra 604. Ib.; Shabbat 149ᵃ (reference. to Vayikra l. common gender.) אל תִּפְנוּ אֶל מדעתכם turn not to the creation of your fancy (Rashi; anoth. interpret., see infra); and see from

—2) to turn around, go away. Eicha Rabbah to I, 1 כיון ששתה ופ׳ לילך (מעשה) רבתי when he had drunk and turned to go away. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 68 יצא משם פ׳ זיוה פ׳ הדרה when he (the righteous) goes away from a place, its splendor is gone, its glory is gone; Ruth Rabbah to I, 7. Sifra K’dosh., Chaldaic VIII, Parah 4, and e. (reference. to ונתתי את פני, Vayikra XX, 6; compare פְּנַאי) פּוֹנֶה אני מכל וכ׳, see עֵסֶק. Midrash Mishlei to XVI, 11 לִפְנוֹת היום when the day was going away (towards evening); and see from

—3) (act. verb) to turn, pervert. Shir HaShirim Rabbah to VII, 9 (play on אח̇ש̇ד̇רפ̇נ̇יא, Daniel III, 2) אלו ארכונות שהן נש̇ח̇ד̇ין ופ̇וני̇ן דין וכ׳ (not נחשדין) those are the officers that are bribed and turn justice in any direction; ib. שמה̇ד̇ר̇ין פ̇נ̇ים ופ̇ונ̇ין דין who respect persons and pervert justice; and from

—4) to turn aside, go out, (euphem.) to ease one’s self. Yerushalmi Sotah I, 16ᵈ אם יִפְנֶה אחד מהן לצורכו if one of them goes out for a human need. Toharot X, 2 ופוֹנִים (Berakhot 62ᵃ ונִפְנִין, Nifal).

—5) to vacate (see infra); to free, release. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 42 הספינה … ולא תטריח עליה לִפְנוֹתָהּ (not הטריח) thy friend’s ship has been seized (for public service), and wilt thou not take pains to release it? ועכשיו של אחרים הוא פוֹנֶה ושלו אינה נפנית and now he releases other men’s ships, and shall not his be released.?—Part. pass. פָּנוּי; f. פְּנוּיָה vacant, empty, free. Berakhot 43ᵃ אין בית הבליעה פ׳ his œsophagus is not free (which makes speaking dangerous). Yerushalmi Kilayim III, beginning 28ᶜ אי אפשר … נקב אחד פ׳ וכ׳ it is not possible that there should not be one cavity free for planting &c.; Yerushalmi Shabbat IX, 11ᵈ bottom of page אפשר … פניי (correct accordingly). Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 14 והיה הבית פ׳ and the house was empty (none at home); and from—V. פָּנוּי.

Piël - פִּינָּה
1) to empty, remove, transfer. Shabbat III, 5 המיחם שפִּינָּהוּ וכ׳ in the kettle which one has emptied (or: which one has removed from the oven) &c.; ib. 41ᵃ המיחם שפ׳ ממנו מים וכ׳ in the kettle out of which one has removed the hot water. Ib. XVIII, 1 מְפַנִּין אפי׳ וכ׳ you may clear away (on the Sabbath) even four or five piles … to make room for guests. Yerushalmi Gittin VIII, 49ᵈ top אם … איש מְפַנֶּה if the court belongs to the wife, the husband (after divorce) must vacate it, ושל איש אשה מְפַנָּה and if it belongs to the husband, the wife must vacate it; מי מפנה מפני מי which of them must vacate it for the other? Taanit 21ᵃ בקשו תלמידיו לפַנּוֹת את וכ׳ his disciples wanted to move his bed first and then his furniture; פַּנּוּ את הכלים וכ׳ move the furniture first. Pirkei Avot III, 4 מפנה לבו לבטלה empties his heart (of serious thoughts to make room) for frivolous subjects. Shabbat 149ᵃ (reference. to Vayikra XIX, 4, see supra) אל תְּפַנוּ אֵל מדעתכם do not remove God from your minds (to make room for idols). Bava Kamma 81ᵇ מְפַנֵּיהוּ לשדה וכ׳ he must remove the corpse to &c. Yerushalmi Ma'asrot II, 49ᵈ רוצה אדם לפנות עסקיו וכ׳ (ed. Krot. רוצה הוא אדם לפנע; ed. Zyt. לפלה, correct accordingly) a man is anxious to dispose of his goods in the first place he strikes &c.; and from

—2) to free, acquit. Midrash Tanḥuma Vayikra 6 פ׳ לקרתני ולבן פלטרין וכ׳ he acquitted the commoner, but convicted the courtier. Ib. לקרתני פִּנִּיתִי וכ׳ I acquitted the commoner, because he knows not the royal customs; and from

Nifal - נִפְנֶה
1) to turn. Midrash Till. to Psalms XVIII, 5 נִפְנֵיתִי לכאן וכ׳ I turned in all directions, and there is no redeemer but thee; Yalkut Samuel 157; and e.

—2) to be removed, to die. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 98 שהיה נ׳ מן העולם who was going to die. Tosefta Parah III (II), 8 נ׳ בני my son is dead (see infra); and e.

—3) to be free, at leisure. Ib. לכשאֶפָּנֶה לך when I shall have leisure for thee, i.e. I shall take revenge on thee, when opportunity offers; אמר לו כשתִּפָּנֶה said he to him, when thou shalt be at leisure (or when thou shalt be dead, see supra); ib. (Vers. of Rabbenu Shimshon to Parah III, 8) לא נ׳ בני שהעריב שמשו my son has found no leisure (to take revenge), for his sun has set (he is dead). Pirkei Avot II, 4 אל תאמר לכשאפנה אשנה שמא לא תפנה say not, when I shall be at leisure, I will study; may be thou wilt never find leisure; and from

—4) to ease one’s self. Shabbat 82ᵃ הנצרך לִפָּנוֹת ואינו נפנה (Hilkhot Rabbeinu Alfasi להִפָּנוֹת) he who feels the want of easing himself, and is not relieved; ib. הנצרך ליפנות ואינו יכול ליפנות. Berakhot 62ᵃ ונִפְנִין, see supra; and from

—5) to be released. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. l. common gender., see supra.

Hifil - הִפְנָה to vacate. —Part. pass. מוּפְנֶה a) free, disengaged, single. Yevamot III, 5 שלשה אחין … ואחד מ׳ three brothers two of whom were married to two sisters, and one is free (unmarried or married to one who is a stranger to his brothers’ wives); Yerushalmi ib. III, 4ᵈ top; and e.—b) (dialectical exegesis) free for interpretation, unnecessary for the plain sense or context. Niddah 22ᵇ וייצר מ׳ משני צדדין מ׳ … ומ׳ גבי בהמה vayitser is free for interpretation on both sides, it is free with regard to man (Breishit II, 7, because man’s creation is mentioned in ויברא, ib. I, 27), and free with regard to beasts (ib. II, 19, their creation being stated in ויעש, ib. I, 25). Ib. כל גזירה שוה שאינה מוּפְנָה כל עיקר וכ׳ analogous words which are not entirely free (in both texts) cannot be made the basis for interpretation as g’zerah shavah (see גְּזֵרָה). Ib. מ׳ מצד אחד free in one of the texts; Shabbat 64ᵃ; and from

Hithpaël - הִתְפַּנָּה
1) to be vacated, cleared, removed. Yerushalmi Nazir IX, 57ᵈ bottom of page כל הקברות מִתְפַּנִּין וכ׳ all graves may be vacated (transferred), except &c.; Masechet Masechet Smachot Chaldaic XIV.

—2) to be released. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. l. common gender. כדי הוא (ש)תִּיתְפִּנֶּה he deserves it to have his ship released (ed. Prag כדי הוא שיִתְפַּנֶּה he deserves to be released).

With regard to where one may or may not go to defecate, Ulla said: Behind a fence, one need not distance himself from people and may defecate immediately. In a valley or open field, one must distance himself sufficiently so that if he passes wind, no one will hear him. Isi bar Natan taught as follows: Behind a fence one must distance himself sufficiently so that if he passes wind another does not hear him, and in a valley, one must distance himself sufficiently so that no one can see him.

The Gemara raises an objection based on what we learned in a mishna in Teharot: Physical laborers, who usually fall into the category of am ha’aretz and are not generally cautious with regard to the laws of ritual purity, exit from the entrance of the olive press, defecate behind the fence, and are ritually pure. There is no reason to be concerned that they might become impure in the interim. This indicates that a greater distance is unnecessary.
The Gemara responds: With regard to the laws of ritual purity, they were lenient. To ensure maintenance of purity, they were lenient and did not require a greater distance.

Come and hear from what we learned: How far may workers distance themselves, and the fruit and oil will remain pure? They may distance themselves only so far that he still sees him. This contradicts the opinion of Isi bar Natan, who required them to distance themselves sufficiently that they may not be seen. The Gemara responds: Those who eat in purity are different, as the Sages were lenient with them.

Rav Ashi said: What is the meaning of: So long as another does not see him, which was the standard that Isi bar Natan said? Sufficient that another person cannot see his nakedness, although he does see him.

The Gemara relates: There was a particular eulogizer who went to eulogize an important person in the presence of Rav Naḥman. Of the deceased, he said: This man was modest in his ways. Rav Naḥman said to him: Did you go to the bathroom with him and know whether or not he was modest? As we learned in a baraita: One can only describe as modest one who is modest even in the bathroom, when no one else is there.

The Gemara asks: And what difference did it make to Rav Naḥman, that he was so insistent upon the details of whether or not this man was modest? The Gemara answers: Because it was taught in a baraita: Just as the deceased are punished, so too are the eulogizers and those who answer after them.The deceased are punished for transgressions committed in their lifetimes. The eulogizers and those who answer are punished for accepting the attribution of virtues that the deceased did not possess.
he: אָמַר עוּלָּא: אֲחוֹרֵי הַגָּדֵר — נִפְנֶה מִיָּד. וּבַבִּקְעָה, כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁמִּתְעַטֵּשׁ וְאֵין חֲבֵרוֹ שׁוֹמֵעַ. אִיסִי בַּר נָתָן מַתְנֵי הָכִי: אֲחוֹרֵי הַגָּדֵר, כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁמִּתְעַטֵּשׁ וְאֵין חֲבֵרוֹ שׁוֹמֵעַ, וּבַבִּקְעָה — כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁאֵין חֲבֵרוֹ רוֹאֵהוּ.
מֵיתִיבִי: יוֹצְאִין מִפֶּתַח בֵּית הַבַּד, וְנִפְנִין לַאֲחוֹרֵי הַגָּדֵר, וְהֵן טְהוֹרִין!
תָּא שְׁמַע: כַּמָּה יַרְחִקוּ וְיִהְיוּ טְהוֹרִין — כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהֵא רוֹאֵהוּ! שָׁאנֵי אוֹכְלֵי טְהָרוֹת, דַּאֲקִילּוּ בְּהוּ רַבָּנַן.
רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: מַאי ״כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁאֵין חֲבֵרוֹ רוֹאֶה״ דְּקָאָמַר אִיסִי בַּר נָתָן — כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁאֵין חֲבֵרוֹ רוֹאֶה אֶת פֵּרוּעוֹ, אֲבָל לְדִידֵיהּ חָזֵי לֵיהּ.

הַהוּא סַפְדָנָא דִּנְחֵית קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן, אֲמַר: ״הַאי צָנוּעַ בְּאוֹרְחוֹתָיו הֲוָה״. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן: אַתְּ עֲיַילְתְּ בַּהֲדֵיהּ לְבֵית הַכִּסֵּא וְיָדְעַתְּ אִי צָנוּעַ אִי לָא? דְּתַנְיָא: אֵין קוֹרִין ״צָנוּעַ״ אֶלָּא לְמִי שֶׁצָּנוּעַ בְּבֵית הַכִּסֵּא.
וְרַב נַחְמָן מַאי נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִינֵּיהּ? מִשּׁוּם דְּתַנְיָא: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁנִּפְרָעִין מִן הַמֵּתִים כָּךְ נִפְרָעִין מִן הַסַּפְדָנִין, וּמִן הָעוֹנִין אַחֲרֵיהֶן.

comments.en: A child was found next to dough with a piece of dough in his hand: Rabbi Meir says that the dough is clean; But the sages say that it is unclean, since it is the nature of a child to slap dough. Dough that bears traces of hens’ pickings and there is unclean liquid in the same house: if there was distance enough between the liquid and the loaves for the hens to dry their mouths on the ground, the dough is clean. And in the case of a cow or a dog, if there was distance enough for it to lick its tongue. And in the case of all other beasts, if there was distance enough for their tongue to dry. Rabbi Eliezer ben Jacob holds the dough to be clean in the case of a dog who is smart; for it is not its habit to leave food and go after the water.
comments.he: תִּינוֹק שֶׁנִּמְצָא בְצַד הָעִסָּה וְהַבָּצֵק בְּיָדוֹ, רַבִּי מֵאִיר מְטַהֵר. וַחֲכָמִים מְטַמְּאִים, שֶׁדֶּרֶךְ הַתִּינוֹק לְטַפֵּחַ. בָּצֵק שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ נְקִירַת תַּרְנְגוֹלִים, וּמַשְׁקִין טְמֵאִין בְּתוֹךְ הַבַּיִת, אִם יֵשׁ בֵּין מַשְׁקִין לַכִּכָּרוֹת כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּנַגְּבוּ אֶת פִּיהֶם בָּאָרֶץ, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ טְהוֹרִין. וּבְפָרָה וּבְכֶלֶב, כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּלַחֲכוּ אֶת לְשׁוֹנָם. וּשְׁאָר כָּל הַבְּהֵמָה, כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּתְנַגֵּב. רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב מְטַהֵר בְּכֶלֶב, שֶׁהוּא פִקֵּחַ, שֶׁאֵין דַּרְכּוֹ לְהַנִּיחַ אֶת הַמָּזוֹן וְלֵילֵךְ לַמָּיִם:

sections.en: If the olive-workers in an olive-press went in and out, and in the olive-press there was unclean liquid, if there is space enough [on the ground] between the liquid and the olives for their feet to be dried on the ground, the olive workers remain clean. If something unclean was found in front of olive-workers in the olive-press or grape harvesters, they are believed to say, "We have not touched it." And the same law applies also to the young children among them. They may go outside the door of the olive-press and relieve themselves behind the wall, and still be deemed clean. How far may they go and still be deemed clean? As far as they can be seen.
sections.he: הַבַּדָּדִין שֶׁהָיוּ נִכְנָסִין וְיוֹצְאִין, וּמַשְׁקִין טְמֵאִין בְּתוֹךְ בֵּית הַבַּד, אִם יֵשׁ בֵּין מַשְׁקִין לַזֵּיתִים כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּנַגְּבוּ אֶת רַגְלֵיהֶם בָּאָרֶץ, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ טְהוֹרִין. הַבַּדָּדִין וְהַבּוֹצְרִין שֶׁנִּמְצֵאת טֻמְאָה לִפְנֵיהֶם, נֶאֱמָנִין לוֹמַר לֹא נָגָעְנוּ. וְכֵן הַתִּינוֹקוֹת שֶׁבֵּינֵיהֶם, יוֹצְאִים חוּץ לְפֶתַח בֵּית הַבַּד וּפוֹנִין לַאֲחוֹרֵי הַגָּדֵר, וְהֵן טְהוֹרִין. עַד כַּמָּה יַרְחִיקוּ וְיִהְיוּ טְהוֹרִין, עַד כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהֵא רוֹאָן:

sections.en: If the olive-workers or the grape harvesters were only brought within the domain of the cavern, it is sufficient, the words of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Yose says: he should stand over them until they immerse. Rabbi Shimon say: if they regard the vessels as clean, one must stand over them until they immerse; but if they regard them as unclean, it is not necessary to stand over them until they immerse.
sections.he: הַבַּדָּדִין וְהַבּוֹצְרִין, כֵּיוָן שֶׁהִכְנִיסָן לִרְשׁוּת הַמְּעָרָה, דַּיּוֹ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, צָרִיךְ לַעֲמֹד עֲלֵיהֶן עַד שֶׁיִּטְבֹּלוּ. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, אִם טְהוֹרִין לָהֶן, צָרִיךְ לַעֲמֹד עֲלֵיהֶם עַד שֶׁיִּטְבֹּלוּ. אִם טְמֵאִים לָהֶן, אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לַעֲמֹד עֲלֵיהֶם עַד שֶׁיִּטְבֹּלוּ:

en: מִשְׁטֵחַ, מִשְׁטֵיחַ m. (Biblical Hebrew spreading, grapes spread on the ground; spreading place. Toharot X, 4 הנותן … ומן המ׳ של אדמה he who puts in the press grapes collected in baskets or such as were spread on the (naked) ground; ib. מן המ׳ של עלים grapes spread on leaves. Tosefta ib. XI, 8. Y’lamdenu (a lost book, corresponding to Tanḥuma, quoted in Arukh) to Bamidbar VII, 1 ממלא מִשְׁטֵחוֹ he fills his spreading place.—plural מִשְׁטֵחִים, מִשְׁטֵחִין, מִשְׁטֵי׳ layers. Sifré Bamidbar 98 שהיתה עשויה מ׳ מ׳ the quails formed layers; Yoma 75ᵇ

עָבִיט m. (עבט, see עֲבוֹט; compare חֶבֶט I) [fastening, pressing,]
1) (של גמל) sumpter-saddle consisting of a pair of panniers tied across the animal’s back (Lat. clitellae, Gr. κανθήλια); also the cushion on the camel’s back (Arab. gabiṭ). Sifra M’tsor‘a, Zavim, Parah 2, Chaldaic III; Kelim XXIII, 2; and e.—plural עֲבִיטִין. Tosefta Eruvin III (II), 1; Eruvin 16ᵃ top; Yerushalmi ib. I, 19ᵇ bottom of page—Midrash Tanḥuma Emor 18 עביטות. see עֲבוֹט.

—2) ע׳ של ענבים (compare κανθήλια) a large basket, strapped on the carrier’s back, in which grapes are carried during the vintage. Bava Metzia V, 7 (72ᵇ); Tosefta ib. VI, 2. Tosefta Ma'asrot III, 13 (ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) עבוט, correct accordingly). Tosefta Demai VI, 11; Yerushalmi ib. VI, 25ᶜ bottom of page עֶבֶט. Yerushalmi Beitzah V, beginning 62ᵈ העבט. Toharot X, 4, sq. העביט ed. Dehr. (ed. העבט; Arukh מעבט). Yerushalmi Moʿed Katan II, beginning 81ᵃ דורכין את עַבְטוֹ you may press, for the mourner, the grapes in the basket (to prevent ruin by delay); and e.

—3) ע׳ של מימי רגלים a large vessel for the collection of urine (for manufacturing purposes). Berakhot 25ᵇ גרף של רעי וע׳ וכ׳ a vessel for the collection of excrements, and a tub for urine; Tosefta ib. II, 16 Variant Bava Batra 89ᵇ.—Ketubot 82ᵇ, read with Tosafot: ע׳ של נחושת a bronze tub.

sections.en: One who puts his grapes [into the wine-press] from the baskets or from what was spread out on the ground: Bet Shammai says: he must put them in with clean hands, and if he puts them in with unclean hands he defiles them. Bet Hillel says: he may put them in with unclean hands and then he may set aside his terumah in a condition of cleanness. [If they are taken] from the grape-pot or from what was spread out on leaves, all agree that they must be put in with clean hands, and if they are put in with unclean hands they become unclean.
sections.he: הַנּוֹתֵן מִן הַסַּלִּים וּמִן הַמַּשְׁטֵחַ שֶׁל אֲדָמָה, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, נוֹתֵן בְּיָדַיִם טְהוֹרוֹת. וְאִם נָתַן בְּיָדַיִם טְמֵאוֹת, טִמְּאָן. בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, נוֹתֵן בְּיָדַיִם טְמֵאוֹת, וּמַפְרִישׁ תְּרוּמָתוֹ בְּטָהֳרָה. מִן הָעֲבַט וּמִן הַמַּשְׁטֵחַ שֶׁל עָלִים, הַכֹּל שָׁוִים שֶׁהוּא נוֹתֵן בְּיָדַיִם טְהוֹרוֹת. וְאִם נָתַן בְּיָדַיִם טְמֵאוֹת, טִמְּאָן:

en:
חוֹתָם m. (Biblical Hebrew; חָתַם)
1) seal, stamp, die; enclosure locked up with a mark. Shabbat VIII, 5 כח׳ המרצופין as much sealing clay as required for a seal on bags. Ib. ח׳ האיגרות seal on letters. Sanhedrin IV, 5 אדם טובע … בח׳ אחד a human being prints many coins from one die &c., but the Lord טבע … בחוֹתָמוֹ של וכ׳ stamped every human being with the die of Adam, and yet not one is like the other; Yerushalmi ib. IV, 22ᵇ bottom of page מח׳ וכ׳. Shabbat 58ᵃ העבד בח׳ שבצוארו the slave with the mark hanging down from his neck, בח׳ שבכסותו with the mark tied to his garment; and from—Transferred sexual innocence; purity. Yalkut Bamidbar 766, see infra.—plural חוֹתָמוֹת, חוֹתָמִים. Yerushalmi Sanhedrin l. common gender.—Beitzah 31ᵇ ח׳ שבקרקע וכ׳ knots which serve as marks on doors of subterranean stores, may be untied &c.; and e.—Tan. d’be El. Chaldaic XX, בחוֹתָמֵיהֶן in their innocence.

—2) [lock,] the oblate side of a berry to which the stalk is attached. Yerushalmi Pirkei Avot Zar. V, 44ᵈ top. Toharot X, 5 גרגר … ח׳ a single berry, if its oblate part with the stalk is intact; Tosefta ib. XI, 10. Ib. מקום ח׳ the place where the stalk (now torn out) was seated (and where now juice is oozing out).

—3) the membraneous enclosure separating the stone of a date from its flesh, pericarp (as far as not eatable). Tosefta Chullin I, 23 הח׳ טמא ביבשה quot. by Rabbenu Shimshon to 'Uktzin II, 2 (ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) הח׳ omitted; oth. ed. הזיתים in place of the preceding העמים) the pericarp is counted in with the unclean matter in dry dates; 'Uktzin l. common gender. ח׳ של יבשה Rabbenu Shimshon (ed. and Maimonides חותל).

—4) concluding formula of prayers.—plural as ab. Taanit II, 3 חוֹתָמֵיהֶן. Yerushalmi Berakhot I, 3ᵈ bottom of page חוֹתְמוֹתֵיהֶן, see חִיתּוּם.
מַעְבֵּט , Toharot X, 5, Arukh, see עָבִיט
מָפְנֶה m. (פָּנָה) vacancy. Toharot X, 5 מקום המ׳ a vacant place.

comments.en: Rabbi Meir says: oil always remains unclean in the first degree. And the sages say: honey also. Rabbi Shimon Shezuri says: also wine. A mass of olives that fell into an oven that was heated: If [the olives] were exactly the size of an egg it [the oven] remains pure; But if it was more than that of an egg the oven becomes unclean, for as soon as the first drop came out it became unclean by contact with an egg's bulk. If the olives were separated even if there was a se'ah of them, it remains clean.
comments.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, הַשֶּׁמֶן תְּחִלָּה לְעוֹלָם. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אַף הַדְּבָשׁ. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שְׁזוּרִי אוֹמֵר, אַף הַיָּיִן. וְגוּשׁ שֶׁל זֵיתִים שֶׁנָּפַל לְתַנּוּר וְהֻסַּק, כַּבֵּיצָה מְכֻוָּן, טָהוֹר. יוֹתֵר מִכַּבֵּיצָה, טָמֵא, שֶׁכֵּיוָן שֶׁיָּצָאת טִפָּה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה, נִטְמֵאת בְּכַבֵּיצָה. אִם הָיוּ פְרוּדִין, אֲפִלּוּ הֵן סְאָה, טָהוֹר:

comments.en: Sauce, bean-mash and milk, when in a condition of fluidity, are unclean in the first degree. If they turned solid they become unclean in the second degree. If they again melted: If their bulk was exactly that of an egg, they are clean. But if it was more than the bulk of an egg they remain unclean, for as soon as the first drop issued forth it became unclean by contact with an egg's bulk.
comments.he: הָרֹטֶב וְהַגְּרִיסִים וְהֶחָלָב, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהֵן מַשְׁקֶה טוֹפֵחַ, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ תְּחִלָּה. קָרְשׁוּ, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ שְׁנִיִּים. חָזְרוּ וְנִמֹּחוּ, כַּבֵּיצָה מְכֻוָּן, טָהוֹר. יוֹתֵר מִכַּבֵּיצָה, טָמֵא, שֶׁכֵּיוָן שֶׁיָּצְאָה טִפָּה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה, נִטְמֵאת בְּכַבֵּיצָה:

הלוקח משטיח של אדמה מישראל לעשותו צמוקין ה"ז עושה זיתים בטהרה. האוכל מן הסלים ומן המשטיח של אדמה אכל והותיר כסאה כסאתים אע"פ שניפצה לגת והיין מגיתו ע"ג ענבים טהור וכן בעובד כוכבים אין חושש משום יי"נ. נפל ממנו גרגר יחידי אם יש לו חותם טהור אין לו חותם טמא בד"א בזמן שנגע במקום חותם טהור ר' יוסי בן כיפר א"ר אלעזר בד"א בזמן שנגע במקום לא נגע במקום המשקה טהור ר' יוסי אומר נפלה הימנו כארבע כחמש ביצים ודרכן כולו בבת אחת משקה היוצאין מהן טהור כיון שדרס עליהן משקין טהרה שאין לו משקין במה יטמא מי שהיה עומד ומדבר ע"פ הבור ונתזה צינורה מפיו ספק הגיע לבור ספק לא הגיע של שמן ספיקו טמא של יין ספיקו טהור מפני שהבל הבור קולטת.

sections.en: One who eats grapes out of the baskets or from what is spread out on the ground, even though they burst and dripped into the wine-press, the wine-press remains clean. If he eats the grapes out of a grape-basket or from what was spread out on leaves, and a single berry dropped into the vat: If it has a seal all in the vat remains clean; But if it has no seal, all in the vat becomes unclean. If he dropped some of the grapes and trod upon them in an empty part of the wine-press: If the bulk of the grapes was exactly that of an egg, the contents remain clean; But if it was more than the bulk of an egg, the contents become unclean, for so soon as the first drop came out it contracted uncleanness from the remainder whose bulk is that of an egg.
sections.he: הָאוֹכֵל מִן הַסַּלִּים וּמִן הַמַּשְׁטֵחַ שֶׁל אֲדָמָה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמְּבֻקָּעוֹת וּמְנַטְּפוֹת לַגַּת, הֲרֵי הַגַּת טְהוֹרָה. מִן הָעֲבַט וּמִן הַמַּשְׁטֵחַ שֶׁל עָלִים וְנָפַל מִמֶּנּוּ גַרְגֵּר יְחִידִי, אִם יֶשׁ לוֹ חוֹתָם, טָהוֹר. אִם אֵין לוֹ חוֹתָם, טָמֵא. נָפְלוּ מִמֶּנּוּ עֲנָבִים וּדְרָכָן בְּמָקוֹם הַמֻּפְנֶה, כַּבֵּיצָה מְכֻוָּן, טָהוֹר. יוֹתֵר מִכַּבֵּיצָה, טָמֵא, שֶׁכֵּיוָן שֶׁיָּצָאת טִפָּה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה, נִטְמֵאת בְּכַבֵּיצָה:

comments.en: If a tree standing in a public domain had within it an object of uncleanness and a man climbed to the top of it, and a doubt arose as to whether he did or did not touch the object of uncleanness, such a condition of doubt is unclean. If one put his hand into a hole [in the wall] in which there was an object of uncleanness and there is doubt whether he did or did not touch it, such a condition of doubt is unclean. If a shop that was unclean was open toward a public domain and there is doubt whether a man did or did not enter it, such a condition of doubt is clean. If there is doubt whether he did or did not touch anything, such a condition of doubt is deemed clean. If there were two shops, the one unclean and the other clean, and a man entered into one of them, and a doubt arose as to whether he entered the unclean, or the clean one, such a condition of doubt is deemed unclean.
comments.he: אִילָן שֶׁהוּא עוֹמֵד בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים וְהַטֻּמְאָה בְתוֹכוֹ, עָלָה לְרֹאשׁוֹ, סָפֵק נָגַע סָפֵק לֹא נָגַע, סְפֵקוֹ טָמֵא. הִכְנִיס יָדוֹ לְחוֹר שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ טֻמְאָה, סָפֵק נָגַע סָפֵק לֹא נָגַע, סְפֵקוֹ טָמֵא. חֲנוּת שֶׁהוּא טָמֵא וּפָתוּחַ לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים, סָפֵק נִכְנַס סָפֵק לֹא נִכְנַס, סְפֵקוֹ טָהוֹר. סָפֵק נָגַע סָפֵק לֹא נָגַע, סְפֵקוֹ טָהוֹר. שְׁתֵּי חֲנֻיּוֹת, אֶחָד טָמֵא וְאֶחָד טָהוֹר, נִכְנַס לְאַחַד מֵהֶן, סָפֵק לַטָּמֵא נִכְנַס סָפֵק לַטָּהוֹר נִכְנַס, סְפֵקוֹ טָמֵא:

הלוקח משטיח של אדמה מישראל לעשותו צמוקין ה"ז עושה זיתים בטהרה. האוכל מן הסלים ומן המשטיח של אדמה אכל והותיר כסאה כסאתים אע"פ שניפצה לגת והיין מגיתו ע"ג ענבים טהור וכן בעובד כוכבים אין חושש משום יי"נ. נפל ממנו גרגר יחידי אם יש לו חותם טהור אין לו חותם טמא בד"א בזמן שנגע במקום חותם טהור ר' יוסי בן כיפר א"ר אלעזר בד"א בזמן שנגע במקום לא נגע במקום המשקה טהור ר' יוסי אומר נפלה הימנו כארבע כחמש ביצים ודרכן כולו בבת אחת משקה היוצאין מהן טהור כיון שדרס עליהן משקין טהרה שאין לו משקין במה יטמא מי שהיה עומד ומדבר ע"פ הבור ונתזה צינורה מפיו ספק הגיע לבור ספק לא הגיע של שמן ספיקו טמא של יין ספיקו טהור מפני שהבל הבור קולטת.

sections.en: One who was standing and speaking by the edge of the cistern and some spittle squirted from his mouth, and there arises the doubt whether it reached the cistern or not, the condition of doubt is regarded as clean.
sections.he: מִי שֶׁהָיָה עוֹמֵד וּמְדַבֵּר עַל שְׂפַת הַבּוֹר וְנִתְּזָה צִנּוֹרָא מִפִּיו, סָפֵק הִגִּיעָה לַבּוֹר סָפֵק לֹא הִגִּיעָה, סְפֵקוֹ טָהוֹר:

en:
זָלַף (compare זלח, דלף)
1) to pour, empty over. Moʿed Katan II, 1, sq. זוֹלֵף וכ׳ he may empty the contents of the vat into the press and finish the process &c. Yerushalmi ib. 81ᵃ bottom of page זוֹלְפִין את יינו they put his grapes for him into the press. Toharot X, 7 הזוֹלֵף את הבור if one empties the wine or oil pit.

—2) to sprinkle. Parah VI, 2 זָלַף וכ׳ (Rabbenu Shimshon זִילֵּף) if he used all the water for sprinkling. Ib. 3 יזלף ed. (comm. זוֹלֵף; Yoma 58ᵃ זולף והולך) he may sprinkle &c. (Bartenura and Rashi to Yoma l. common gender. he may empty the water into bottles &c.). Ib. VII, 8 זולף (Maimonides: he empties &c.); and from

Piël - זִילֵּף to drip, sprinkle. Parah VI, 2, sq., see supra.—Yerushalmi Shabbat IX, 12ᵃ מְזַלְּפִין וכ׳ you may drip hot water on the wound; Tosefta ib. XV (XVI), 4. Shabbat XIX, 3; and e.

Hifil - הִזְלִיף to flow, squirt (neut. verb). Pirkei Avot Zar. 59ᵇ מַזְלִיף (Manuscript Munich מזלף; Tosefta ib. VII (VIII), 5 מנתז).

מַחַץ m. (חָצַץ, see Judges V, 11) [distributor, compare בָּזִיךְ,] ladle for filling vessels out of the well, or the wine- or oil-pit. Parah V, 5 שולי המ׳ the sides of a broken ladle. Pirkei Avot Zar. 74ᵇ; Yerushalmi ib. V, end, 45ᵇ; Tosefta ib. VIII (IX), 1. Toharot X, 7 אם היה זולף מ׳ if he emptied the pit by using a ladle (to pour into the vessels).—plural מַחֲצִין. Tosefta Kelim Bava Kamma VII, 15.—[Fl. to Levy Talmud Dict. III, 309ᵃ: מָחָץ, from מחץ to stir, compare Psalms LXVIII, 24.]

comments.he: הזולף את הבור כל אחת ואחת ונמצא השרץ בראשונה כולן טמאות באחרונה היא טמאה וכולן טהורות באמצעית הימנה ולמטה טמא הימנה ולמעלה טהור בד"א בזמן שבדק ולא כסה או כסה ולא בדק היה בודקן וכסה ונמצא שרץ באחת מהן היא טמאה בלבד.

sections.en: If one is emptying out the cistern [into jars] and a [dead] sheretz was found in the first jar, all the other jars are deemed unclean; but if it was found in the last, only that one is unclean but all the others remain clean. When does this apply? When the wine was drawn directly with each jar, but if it was drawn with a ladle and a [dead] creeping thing was found in one of the jars, it alone is unclean. When does this apply? Only when the man examined [the jars] but did not cover them up or covered them up but did not examine them; But if he both examined them and covered them up and a [dead] creeping thing was found: If in one jar, all the contents of the cistern are deemed unclean. If it was found in the cistern, all its contents are deemed unclean And if it was found in the ladle all the contents of the cistern are deemed unclean.
sections.he: הַזּוֹלֵף אֶת הַבּוֹר, נִמְצָא שֶׁרֶץ בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה, כֻּלָּן טְמֵאוֹת. בָּאַחֲרוֹנָה, הִיא טְמֵאָה וְכֻלָּן טְהוֹרוֹת. אֵימָתַי, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהוּא זוֹלֵף בְּכָל אַחַת וְאַחַת. אֲבָל אִם הָיָה זוֹלֵף בְּמַחַץ, נִמְצָא שֶׁרֶץ בְּאַחַת מֵהֶן, הִיא טְמֵאָה בִּלְבָד. אֵימָתַי, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהוּא בוֹדֵק וְלֹא מְכַסֶּה אוֹ מְכַסֶּה וְלֹא בוֹדֵק. הָיָה בוֹדֵק וּמְכַסֶּה, וְנִמְצָא שֶׁרֶץ, בֶּחָבִית, הַכֹּל טָמֵא. בַּבּוֹר, הַכֹּל טָמֵא. בַּמַּחַץ, הַכֹּל טָמֵא:

en:
חֲשִׂיפָה f. (חָשַׂף, see חֲסַף I)
1) stripping, uncovering. Yerushalmi Berakhot IX, 13ᵃ top חֲשִׂיפַת זרועו the baring of His arm (Isaiah LII, 10).

—2) paring, shavings used for basket work. Tosefta Kilayim III, 14 הח׳ Variant (ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) השופה); Yerushalmi ib. V, end, 30ᵃ השיפה. Tosefta Toharot XI, 16 של ח׳ quot. by R. section (Parashah) to Toharot X, 8 (ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) של השיפה) basket work made of shavings; Pirkei Avot Zar. 75ᵃ של שיפה (ed. Pesachim חש׳). Sukkah 20ᵃ מחצלת של ח׳ Manuscript Munich (ed. שיפה) matting made of etc.; Tosefta ib. I, 10 שיהופא ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) (Variant חשופא, oth. ed. חשי׳).

עִיגּוּל, עִגּ׳ m. (עָגַל)
1) circle. Sukkah 8ᵃ כמה מרובע יותר על הע׳ by how much is a square larger than a tangent circle within it? One fourth; Oholot XII, 6. Nazir 8ᵇ בֵּית עי׳ Arukh (ed. בית עגול) a circular building; Tosefta Negaim VI, 3 בית העגיל ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) (Variant העגל).

—2) a round mould in which figs or grapes are pressed, cake of pressed figs; cake, loaf. Bava Metzia II, 1 (21ᵃ) מצא ע׳ ובתוכו וכ׳ if one finds a cake of figs within which was a piece of earthen ware (as a mark). Ma'asrot I, 8, see חָלַק. Shabbat 93ᵃ top (explained ככר, ib. X, 5) בע׳ של דבילה a cake of figs (too large for one to carry); and from—plural עִיגּוּלִים, עִיגּוּלִין, עִגּ׳. Terumot IV, 8, see מַלְבֵּן. Yerushalmi Hallah I, 57ᵈ bottom of page Toharot X, 8 בין הע׳ לזונין the space between the moulds and the deposit of grape shells (Maimonides; see infra).—Pirkei Avot d’R. N. Chaldaic VI, end היו מביאין את הע׳ וכ׳ (not העגלים, see ed. Schechter note) they took the loaves of bread and sawed them apart and soiled them with mud.

—3) עִיגּוּלֵי הגת, עִגּ׳ weights (clay cylinders) put on the wine press. Shabbat I, 9 טוענין … ע׳ הגת you may put on (the press) the beams of the oil press or the cylinders of the wine press; Tosefta ib. I, 29 ותולין בע׳ הגת (Variant ע׳ הגת) and suspend the weights &c. Toharot l. common gender. בין ע׳ לזוגין between the cylinders &c. (Rabbenu Shimshon; see supra).

—4) in gen. ball, lump.—plural as ab. Sotah 11ᵇ, and e., see נָקַט. Tosefta Mikvaot V, 8 עגולי שלג lumps of snow; and from

עֵקֶל, עִקָּל ) m. (preceding)
1) a bale of loose texture containing the olive pulp to be pressed. Ma'asrot I, 7; Tosefta ib. I, 7 (Variant עוקל). Toharot X, 8; Yerushalmi Pirkei Avot Zar. V, end, 45ᵇ הע׳ של נצרים, see infra. Shabbat 144ᵇ מוחל היוצא מע׳ בית הבד Arukh (ed. מעיקול) the watery fluid which oozes out of the bale made up for the press; (Tosefta Toharot X, 3 מעיקת; Rabbenu Shimshon to Toharot IX, 1 מן שוקת, correct accordingly). Tosefta l. common gender. כינסו ועשאו עיקל (Rabbenu Shimshon l. common gender. שוקת) if he collected the fluid and put it back into the bale. Sanhedrin 26ᵃ יכול לומר לע׳ בית הבד וכ׳ he (who trims vines in the Sabbatical year) may say, I need the twigs to make a bale for the press. Ib. (proverbial expression) הלב יודע אם לע׳ אם לעקלקלות the heart knows whether it is done for ʿekel (a legitimate purpose) or out of ‘ãḳalḳaloth (perverseness); Yerushalmi Sheviit IV, 35ᵃ; Eicha Rabbah to I, 5; and e.—plural עֲקָלִים, עֲקָלִין (or עִקָּ׳). Yerushalmi Sheviit l. common gender. (in Chald. dict.) לע׳ אנא בעי I need the twigs for &c., see supra. Pirkei Avot Zar. 75ᵃ; Tosefta ib. VIII (IX), 3 הע׳ של נצרין וכ׳ bales made of wicker or hemp &c.; Tosefta Toharot XI, 16 הע׳ של נוצרין. Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 15 ע׳ של זיתים olive pulp.

—2) (from its shape) a mass of iron used for ballast. Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia I, 1. Makhshirin V, 7 המים העולים … ובע׳ וכ׳ (ed. Dehr. ובעיקל) water that comes up (and settles) in the hull, on the ballast or on the rudders; [Maim.: in the cavity in the hull made for the reception of drippings from the deck; compare עוּקָה].

sections.en: [The space] between the rollers and grape skins is regarded as a public domain. A vineyard in front of the grape harvesters is deemed to be a private domain and one which is behind the harvesters is deemed to be a public domain. When is this so? When the public enter at one end and go out at the other. The vessels of the olive-press, the wine-press and the basket-press, if they are of wood, need only be dried and they become clean; But if they are of reed grass they must be left unused for twelve months, or they must be scalded in hot water. Rabbi Yose says: if he put them in the current of the river, it is sufficient.
sections.he: בֵּין הָעִגּוּלִים לַזַּגִּין, רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים. כֶּרֶם שֶׁלִּפְנֵי הַבּוֹצְרִים, רְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד. שֶׁלְּאַחַר הַבּוֹצְרִים, רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים. אֵימָתַי, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהָרַבִּים נִכְנָסִים בָּזוֹ וְיוֹצְאִים בָּזוֹ. כְּלֵי בֵית הַבַּד, וְשֶׁל גַּת, וְהָעֵקֶל, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהֵן שֶׁל עֵץ, מְנַגְּבָן וְהֵן טְהוֹרִין. בִּזְמַן שֶׁהֵן שֶׁל גֶּמִי, מְיַשְּׁנָן כָּל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ, אוֹ חוֹלְטָן בְּחַמִּים. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אִם נְתָנָן בְּשִׁבֹּלֶת הַנָּהָר, דַּיּוֹ:
